summary: Today’s pulse tracks Windows Server 2028 public preview bets on a security-first approach, Markwayne Mullin defends move to take government plane to football game amid flight stoppage – US politics live, and Birmingham council granted interim ban on union jacks on lamp-posts. Across Ars Technica, Guardian, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are council, military, and history. In the background, PlayStation suffers widespread network problems hours before release of GTA VI and Hegseth boasts of Maduro’s capture while vowing to deepen US military cooperation with Venezuela keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Windows Server 2028 public preview bets on a security-first approach
headlines.description: Hardened defaults align with DoD standards, but there may be growing pains.

headlines.title: Markwayne Mullin defends move to take government plane to football game amid flight stoppage – US politics live
headlines.description: The secretary of homeland security flew to attend a college game Saturday, after thousands of flights were cancelled CNN reported that officials said the administration underscored that what has happened is not as a result of cyber-attacks but due to the “hardening and upgrading of our systems ”, including “systems being patched, hardware being applied” . Per CNN, an official added: “It’s good the American people are focused on the need to upgrade our legacy systems.”

headlines.title: Birmingham council granted interim ban on union jacks on lamp-posts
headlines.description: High court judge issues order against Raise the Colours over flags on council-owned street furniture The campaign group Raise the Colours has been temporarily banned from placing union jacks on lamp-posts and roundabouts in Birmingham after a legal challenge by the local council. The high court judge Emma Kelly granted an interim injunction banning the placing of all flags on council-owned street furniture without prior permission in a judgment issued on Wednesday, Birmingham city council said.

headlines.title: PlayStation suffers widespread network problems hours before release of GTA VI
headlines.description: Disruption comes at critical moment, with Grand Theft Auto VI one of the most eagerly anticipated titles in history PlayStation has suffered widespread network problems just hours before the release of Grand Theft Auto VI , one of the most eagerly anticipated titles in recent gaming history. The disruption emerged Wednesday, causing frustrated players to flood social media with complaints about failed logins and server connection problems downloading games and updates.

headlines.title: Hegseth boasts of Maduro’s capture while vowing to deepen US military cooperation with Venezuela
headlines.description: The US defense secretary called the former president’s capture the ‘most sophisticated military operation’ in Latin American history Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”. Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

headlines.title: Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
headlines.description: Hamas condemns the incursion, which the Israeli military says is dismantling a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.

headlinePool.title: Shabana Mahmood backs ban on police marching in pride events in uniform
headlinePool.description: Home secretary says ‘routine two-tier policing’ does not exist, but public trust in impartial law enforcement must be restored Shabana Mahmood has backed a ban on police officers marching in pride events in uniform as she said there had been a “few examples” of two-tier policing . Although she said there was no systematic or routine two-tier policing, the home secretary said “a new impartiality standard” was necessary to reverse the fall in the public’s faith in law enforcement.

headlinePool.title: US admits ‘substantial’ change to extradition request translation for leftist activist
headlinePool.description: DoJ cites three examples of alterations from English into Spanish for James ‘Fergie’ Chambers after Guardian report US authorities have admitted altering the translation of an extradition request for James “Fergie” Chambers from English into Spanish, attributing violent and illegal actions to the wealthy activist and philanthropist that were not in the original. Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

headlinePool.title: Ex-Tory MPs barred from shaping Reform UK’s immigration policy, says Zia Yusuf
headlinePool.description: Comments by Reform’s home affairs spokesperson raise questions about unity at top of the party Former Conservative defectors to Reform UK have been barred from shaping the party’s immigration policy, its home affairs spokesperson has claimed, excluding in effect the majority of the party’s MPs. “If you are in the category of being concerned about [former Conservatives being involved in Reform], none of the above are going to be involved in immigration policy or borders policy,” Zia Yusuf told a podcast by the Spectator magazine.

headlinePool.title: Best Buy sells Blu-rays online and in-store again
headlinePool.description: Popular titles like The Odyssey are being “sold & shipped by Best Buy."

headlinePool.title: Muse privacy invasions are freaking out Meta staffers, internal chats show
headlinePool.description: Erratic Muse outputs sharing random bank, bitcoin balances aren’t real, Meta says.

headlinePool.title: Heavy rain and snow predicted in California as ‘atmospheric river’ moves across state
headlinePool.description: Flood advisories issued for much of Bay Area with coastal flooding and heavy surf possible in southern California Heavy rain or snowfall is predicted across California this week, as an “atmospheric river” dumps precipitation across the state. Flood advisories have been issued for much of the Bay Area , according to the National Weather Service (NWS), while southern California may see coastal flooding, heavy surf, wave damage to coastal piers and parking lots , and beach sand erosion.

headlinePool.title: EU ‘to close door’ to talks on long-term UK ties until Burnham has decided on Brexit
headlinePool.description: Diplomats say piecemeal approach of resets is coming to an end and Europe wants clarity on whether Britain wants to reverse its exit The EU will shut the door to discussions with Andy Burnham about the UK’s longer-term relationship with the bloc until the government has decided whether it wants to proceed with reversing Brexit, diplomats have said. European capitals are also warning they have reached the end of the line for piecemeal “reset” summits with the UK and want the prime minister to focus on his next steps domestically before they proceed.

headlinePool.title: FAA administrator urges ‘lay off’ Sean Duffy for the flight stoppage: ‘Blame me’
headlinePool.description: The comments come as the top US transportation official faces scrutiny over his handling of the tech outage crisis The head of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) took responsibility for the nationwide ground stop that affected more than 12,400 flights on Friday, urging people to “lay off” Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary. “I take full responsibility for it,” Bryan Bedford, the FAA administrator, said at an event featuring aviation officials and lawmakers on Wednesday, Politico reported.
